hints.title: Strictly Increasing Suffix Constraint
hints.text: Ending a shelf span at index i taking books[i] books requires taking books[i] - 1 at i - 1, books[i] - 2 at i - 2, and so forth.

hints.title: Bottleneck Shelf Boundaries
hints.text: The decay slope is bounded by preceding shelves where books[j] < books[i] - (i - j).

hints.title: Monotonic Stack Transition
hints.text: Maintain indices with increasing books[i] - i. The top of the stack marks the closest bottleneck shelf.

hints.title: Monotonic Stack DP Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumBooks(self, books: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(books)
        stk = []
        dp = [0] * n
        for i in range(n):
            while stk and books[stk[-1]] - stk[-1] >= books[i] - i:
                stk.pop()
            j = stk[-1] if stk else -1
            cnt = min(books[i], i - j)
            first_val = books[i] - cnt + 1
            sum_books = cnt * (first_val + books[i]) // 2
            dp[i] = (dp[j] if j != -1 else 0) + sum_books
            stk.append(i)
        return max(dp)
```

complexity.notes: Each shelf index is pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating backward slopes per shelf takes quadratic O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Stores DP array and monotonic stack.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Transforms the decreasing arithmetic progression boundary condition to a monotonic stack problem.
